brief: A tool caddy with a carry handle and divided bins for screws and bits.

requirements.requirement: A tool caddy: a portable cluster of storage cells
requirements.evidence: Three full cells with bins in a compact triangle, 18 parts, joints bolted together.

Two grab handles (hex-acc-handle) on opposite ends, at 0,0 slot 3 and 1,0 slot 0. They are on the sides, not a handle over the top: the top-handle part had nowhere to fit. The configurator cannot say how much weight they hold.
Two bins with 3 compartments each (bin:0,0,0 and bin:1,-1,0), shown holding M3 screws, nuts and standoffs.
bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 has 2 compartments for bits and drivers. With no bit prop available, a hex key set and standoffs stand in.

requirements.requirement: Open faces capped so contents stay in
requirements.evidence: All open side faces have end caps; check_build reports no OPEN_CAP_FACE.

finish.summary: I built a tool caddy from three hex cells joined in a triangle, using 18 parts. Two cells hold full-depth bins with 3 compartments each, for screws, nuts and standoffs. The third cell holds a full-depth bin with 2 compartments, for bits and drivers. Grab handles are fitted on opposite ends, the open side faces are capped and the joints are bolted together. The configurator found no rule errors and no parts overlapping. One limit: there is no handle on top. The top-handle part (the trinity handle insert) had nowhere to fit on this build, so these are side grab handles you lift by. The props are only for display. The catalogue has no driver-bit prop, so a hex key set and a pile of standoffs stand in for bits in the 2-compartment bin. The configurator only checks fit and collisions, so nothing here shows how much weight the caddy can carry when full.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

parts.use: Reaches across a whole triangle of studs, so a lift is shared between recesses instead of hanging off one, and the cell can be carried loaded.
